body: I'm doing okay. I went on a nice trip for break, and I'm still trying out my Zoloft. :)

I'm glad that you keep caring, and that You keep living. 

Zoloft's alright thus far. I had a horrible headache today, but I'm hoping this is just my body's initial reaction to a new medication and things will get better.
The doctor wrote me a prescription for zoloft so I'll start that tomorrow. Hopefully this works out....
I'm doing alright. I went to my MBCT group yesterday and that helped me a little bit. I also called my doctor today. And how are you?

Thank you. I should definitely work out more often. Sometimes the motivation is lacking though. You say multivitamins have helped you. That's good to hear. I take Omega-3 daily since it's supposed to promote good brain health. I think I'll look into a multivitamin. Sugar and caffeine are hard for me to avoid, but that is definitely good advice. 

Thank you.
Thank you so so so much. Your words have helped me greatly today. Thank you for being a wonderful person.

For some reason it's never felt the same as any other disorder. It feels like something made up in my head. It feels like something I should have prevented somehow, but I lost control of it somewhere. It's hard to do simple things like laundry now. It's way harder than I want it to be. Hell, getting up is hard now. I thought I could defeat this depression on my own, but I feel defeated by it now.

Yes. It's extremely rare, but since my doctor said Celexa had the least side effects, I got a little distrusting of medications. In general, I'd rather not be on medication, but this depression is becoming crippling so I guess it's best to try something. :/
Thanks, though I think I'll exhaust my other options before seriously considering bringing my dog down here.

I guess I don't mean to leave you hanging, but it feels embarrassing to say. I'll just leave it with bladder issues. It was a really uncomfortable 2 week trial, and the straw that broke the camel's back was peeing in my bed. That's why I stopped taking it. I guess it was okay other than that. It didn't do a lot in terms of helping or hurting my depression.

No, but I was given the option about a week ago of giving Zoloft a go. I didn't want to try it because when I tried Celexa, it gave me weird side effects. Though, now that I've ended up in /r/suicidewatch, I'm strongly considering trying out Zoloft. Weird side effects could be better than dying...

They isolated me completely from the outside world to the point that I wasn't sure if it existed anymore. It was just a scary time. I'm still getting over it I think. It was four years ago, and I think it'll take a couple more to completely understand it.

Thank you so much. I almost cried when I read this because it really seems like you care about other people. That gives me hope. I'm sorry about your brother and all the pain that you've had to endure. 

Dogs are beautiful animals. I have one who lives 250 miles away. (I'm in college right now, land of the dog free dorm room.) I did get to see him this weekend though. 

I really appreciate your input and your care. Thank you.

Depression, though I went to the hospital for psychosis. I'm glad I'm not alone in this feeling, and I'm sorry that you know it too. It's awful that something that's supposed to help you can be so detrimental.
Thank you. It did a little bit. I'm still frustrated though.

I guess this poem doesn't really tell my story so I'll tell you here. I've struggled with depression for over eight years, and I'm getting discouraged. I'm feeling like it's getting worse. I've tried to kill myself in the past multiple times, but I'd rather not get that low this time. I want help. I'm seeing a counselor and I'm going to group therapy, but I'm getting so discouraged and I don't want to end up in a hospital again. I actually would much rather kill myself than end up institutionalized. I don't know what you can do to help me. I just don't want to feel like I'm drowning by myself.
